article_sentences: Guwahati: As preparations for Durga Puja gather pace across Assam, the inspiring story of a differently abled artisan from Cachar district has captured attention.
Montu Pal, a resident of Siddheswar village in Katigorah, has been crafting Durga idols for the past 18 years, overcoming severe physical challenges through determination and dedication to his art.
Pal lost both his legs in a horrific train accident several years ago.
While the tragedy could have shattered his spirit, it failed to diminish his passion for idol-making.
Undeterred by his physical limitations, he continued his artistic journey, working on his knees and crawling to shape clay into beautifully crafted idols.
Throughout this challenging journey, Pal has received unwavering support from his family.
His wife and children have stood firmly by his side, assisting him at every stage of the idol-making process.
Their contribution has enabled him to continue pursuing his craft despite the difficulties he faces.
This year, Pal has created 16 Durga idols entirely by hand for the upcoming festival, reflecting his exceptional craftsmanship and perseverance.
However, rising prices of raw materials have added to his financial difficulties.
The cost of essential materials, including paint, bamboo, straw, sand and clay, has reportedly nearly doubled, significantly increasing the expenses involved in making the idols.
Despite these challenges, Pal remains committed to his work.

article_sentences: RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha has approached the Supreme Court challenging the constitutional validity of Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, terming it a "fraud" on the Constitution.

Section 16 bars every Court in the country from entertaining or continuing any civil or criminal proceeding against any person who is or was a Chief Election Commissioner or Election Commissioner, for anything done "or purporting" to be done in the discharge of official duty.

Jha has stated that Section 16 confers on unelected officials a shield/blanket immunity which is not even extended to the President, Governor, Member of Parliament, State Legislature, or any judge of the Supreme Court or the High Court, because the immunity extends for a lifetime.
This was added through an amendment in 2023, which had also removed the pro tem arrangement made by the Supreme Court in Anoop Baranwal.

Union of India(2023) for the appointment of the CEC by a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or the leader of the largest opposition party), and the Chief Justice of India.
The 2023 Act had removed the CJI and added a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.

Jha's petition argues: "Parliament, by a late official amendment to an ordinary Bill, has handed the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners a protection wider than all of them: civil and criminal, during office and for life after it, with no carve-out for corruption, mala fides or crime, and with no authority anywhere empowered to lift it."
Jha has stated that Section 16, added through an amendment, is a fraud on the Constitution because it was not originally provided in the Act.
He has said that wherever the Constitutional framers thought fit to provide functional immunity, it has done so and that too only till the person is holding the office.
Per contra, no such immunity was provided under Section 324 of the Constitution for the protection of the Election Commission.
"Section 16 nonetheless confers a constitutional-grade immunity, larger than any the Constitution grants or permits, through a simple majority statute.
It does so under the label of "conditions of service" in an Act whose long title speaks only of "appointment, conditions of service and term of office" and "transaction of business".

stories.headline: Jio taps stock markets for Rs30,200 crore in landmark IPO
stories.title: Jio taps stock markets for Rs30,200 crore in landmark IPO
stories.summary: As Jio Platforms heads to the stock markets to raise around Rs30,200 crore, the public offering marks more than just another large issue in India. It is a stock market debut of a digital service company which transformed India's telecom industry, accelerated the country's digital adoption and emerged as one of the most valuable businesses within the Reliance Industries ecosystem.Jio Platforms has formally kicked off its public market journey by filing its red herring prospectus, with the IPO scheduled to open on October 21 and close on October 23. The offering comprises a fresh issue of 27 crore shares. The Mukesh Ambani-led company aims to raise around Rs30,200 crore with a price band set at Rs1,065-1,119 per piece, positioning it among the biggest IPOs ever in India.Unlike most marquee IPOs, where early investors and promoters use the listing to partially monetise their holdings, Jio Platforms' Rs30,200-crore offering is an entirely fresh issue. Which means existing shareholders will not sell any shares through the IPO, instead the entire proceeds will be used by the company. A large part of the funds—up to Rs27,500 crore—will be used to pare debt at Reliance Jio Infocomm, while the balance will support general corporate requirements and future growth initiatives.Over the years, Jio Platforms has attracted an array of bluechip global investors, including Meta, Google, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, KKR-backed Omicron Asia Holdings, General Atlantic Singapore, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority-backed Platinum Jasmine and TPG-managed India Markets. However, Reliance Industries continues to hold a controlling 66.43 percent stake in the company, retaining a firm grip over the group's most valuable digital asset.According to estimates by Bineet Banka and Abhishek Bhandari, analysts at Nomura, after the potential listing, Reliance’s 66.4 percent stake will be worth Rs481-506 per share which is 41 to 43 percent of the current share price. They say that the upper band of the issue price implies an equity valuation of Rs9.8-10.3 lakh crore.Also Read: Telecom tariffs back in focus as Airtel and Jio take divergent paths“Adding FY26 net debt of Rs1.4 lakh crore (including deferred spectrum liability of Rs1 lakh crore and lease liabilities), and netting the IPO cash, gives an enterprise value of Rs10.9-11.4 lakh crore,” Banka and Bhandari explain.The IPO offers investors a chance to participate in the growth of a business that serves hundreds of millions of users. Since its launch in 2016, Jio Platforms has transformed India's telecom landscape with ultra-cheap data plan, reshaped consumer behaviour and played a pivotal role in bringing millions of Indians online.“We believe that following its listing, Jio will likely need to demonstrate growth to public shareholders. And, with the period of easy subscriber gains likely ending, tariff hikes might become the primary driver of earnings growth,” Banka and Bhandari say.Also Read: Airtel turnaround: How Gopal Vittal rebuilt the telecom giantIndia's telecom sector is now largely a three-horse race between Reliance Jio, Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea. The industry's structure was fundamentally reshaped by Jio's entry in 2016, which triggered a brutal tariff war that led to consolidation and the exit of several operators. While Jio and Airtel have strengthened their market positions through scale, spectrum holdings and aggressive 5G rollouts, Vodafone Idea continues to battle a heavy debt burden, subscriber losses and the need for substantial capital expenditure to expand and upgrade its network.Meanwhile, Jio Platforms' proposed offering is set to become India's largest ever IPO, overtaking Hyundai Motor India's Rs27,800-crore issue in 2024. The rest in the pecking order are National Stock Exchange (Rs22,563 crore), LIC (Rs21,000-crore and Paytm (Rs18,300-crore).

stories.headline: India’s alternative-stay market set to grow 21 percent annually through FY29
stories.title: India’s alternative-stay market set to grow 21 percent annually through FY29
stories.summary: India’s alternative accommodation market is projected to grow at an annual rate of 21.2 percent through FY29. Rising tourism demand puts pressure on the country’s supply of rooms, thereby creating opportunities for homestays, villas and holiday homes.The segment’s gross booking value (GBV) is expected to rise to Rs415.1 billion in FY29, from Rs233.1 billion in FY26, according to How India Travels 2026, a report by online travel platform Booking.com and travel research and advisory firm VIDEC Consultants. Alternative accommodation accounted for around 13 percent of India’s lodging market by GBV in FY26, according to the report released on Thursday. The number of digitally distributed listings in the segment more than doubled, from 102,200 in FY23 to 215,000 in FY26.Travellers in India continue to make plans for October-December despite economic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions and higher airfares. But they are becoming more selective about where they go, how much they spend and how far in advance they book, says Laura Houldsworth, managing director for Asia-Pacific at Booking.com.Also Read: War, currency, fuel prices: Why summer holiday plans are shot“Uncertainty is a big driver. But also think that the desire to travel more frequently also leads into that,” Houldsworth tells Forbes India. Travellers planning one major holiday a year tend to book well in advance, she adds, while those taking several shorter breaks are more likely to plan spontaneously. “India has the shortest booking window globally.”A gap in accommodation supplyThe report found that the average booking window for alternative accommodation shortened from 15 days in FY23 to 12 days in FY26. Online searches for alternative accommodation grew 6 percent between FY24 and FY25, compared with 2 percent for hotels.At the report launch in New Delhi, Suman Billa, additional secretary and director general at the Ministry of Tourism, said the growth in tourism was putting pressure on the country’s existing accommodation capacity. “The demand is exploding, but the supply side is not keeping up,” he said. Citing the rise in domestic tourism visits and international tourist arrivals, Billa said even with new hotels in the pipeline, additional accommodation would be needed to meet demand. “There’s a big opportunity to bring homestays, bed and breakfasts, the alternative accommodation, to step into this gap.”Also Read: Gyms, myths, music: Skyscanner report highlights new travel trends among IndiansExpanding supply is not the only challenge. Billa pointed to inconsistent service standards at smaller properties, where the absence of staff can affect the guest experience. “One of the issues is, of course, standards of service delivery,” said Billa. “It doesn’t have the same backup systems as a hotel does.”Santosh Kumar, regional head, South Asia at Booking.com, said alternative accommodation was also helping spread tourism beyond established destinations. “It’s opening up a plethora of new destinations within the country. It’s helping balance tourism to a large extent, moving traffic away from our most commonly visited destinations,” he said.Also Read: Consumer brands moving into travelShorter booking windows, tighter budgetsThe growth in travel is taking place alongside pressure on household budgets. Airfares have risen ahead of the festive season as airlines contend with higher fuel costs and longer routes due to airspace restrictions amid the West Asia conflict. “Indians are definitely price sensitive. A few dollars can swing a decision for sure,” says Houldsworth.Flight and accommodation prices, however, do not always move in the same direction. Airlines typically offer lower fares earlier to fill seats, with prices rising as departure approaches. Hotels may lower rates closer to the date if rooms remain unoccupied. But for larger properties, such as villas or accommodation for an extended family, prices can rise as availability becomes limited.Booking.com’s search data suggests interest in travel remains strong ahead of the peak season. Searches for domestic accommodation for October-December were up 18 percent year-on-year, while those for international travel rose by 13 percent.“The opportunity to explore home countries is becoming more exciting, more interesting, because these alternative locations, alternative types of experiences are becoming more available,” she says.Houldsworth also points to better roads and increased domestic flight capacity as factors giving travellers more options for shorter trips. Domestic travel, she says, was growing faster than international travel.Beyond India, destinations across East and Southeast Asia are also attracting more travellers. “Intra-regional travel within Asia Pacific is the fastest-growing corridor globally,” Houldsworth says. Asked about the factors behind the shift towards Asia-Pacific, she says, “Cost is definitely an impact,” adding that economic conditions were challenging for many countries and travellers. Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia are among the destinations benefiting from this shift.“Intergenerational travel is also very strong in Asia,” she says. “That also gives rise to staying, maybe not going too far, if you’re travelling with three generations and maybe 10-plus people.”

stories.headline: Big items done, confident we will have India-US trade deal: Sergio Gor
stories.title: Big items done, confident we will have India-US trade deal: Sergio Gor
stories.summary: The US and India have resolved the major issues in their proposed trade agreement, with a final deal expected after the two sides work through the remaining details, US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said, even as Washington weighs potential tariffs on countries buying Russian oil.“I am confident we will have a trade deal here,” Gor said at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi on Thursday. “The big picture, the big framework, the big items are done.”India faced tariffs as high as 50 percent at one point last year, which were brought down to 18 percent when the two sides agreed on a framework for a deal in February this year. “We had a trade deal. Within three weeks of [Gor’s] arriving here, we announced a trade deal,” Gor said.The US Supreme Court then ruled that the tariffs were unconstitutional. “The administration has had to go back and rework some of those things. So we’re getting there,” he added. Gor declined to provide a date for the agreement or identify the remaining sticking points.Also Read: India sees no problem in any agreements with US: Piyush GoyalThe ambassador said the negotiations were unusually detailed, reflecting the scale and complexity of the two economies. “I’ve been in multiple of these trade negotiations rooms with Ambassador [Jamieson] Greer and Minister [Piyush] Goyal here from India. They’re literally discussing percentages of products. It’s down to that kind of detail,” he explained.India signed a trade deal with the European Union earlier this year, which was concluded after 20 years of negotiations. India and the US have been in talks for one-and-a-half years. “We’re at an incredible pace, and I would say almost an unheard-of pace. And I’m confident that we’ll get it done.”Another piece of uncertainty for India amid the trade deal talks is a legislation passed by the US Congress that gives Trump the authority to impose tariffs of as much as 100 percent on countries purchasing Russian oil and gas, including India. A decision on that will come “within the next 10 or so days”, Gor said, adding that the goal is not to punish anyone, it’s to end the war.Trump signed the Bill on September 18 and according to US Congress rules, he has 30 days from the signing date to decide on the implementation. That means the deadline is in three days.Also Read: What does a delayed US trade deal mean for India?India has repeatedly defended its decision to buy oil from any region, saying that it has the right to ensure the energy security of its 1.4 billion people.Asked whether India could receive sanctions relief or an exemption, Gor said “that’s a decision for the president”.Following his signing of the law, Trump last week announced a deal to buy diesel from Russia.‘Unmatched’ market in IndiaGor highlighted Reliance Industries’ plans for a new refinery in the US, describing it as the first such project in the country in 50 years.“We’re very proud because they’re opening the first refinery in the United States in 50 years. So that is something that has not happened in many decades. It’s happening with this administration because we’ve engaged,” he said.The amount of investment that we’ve seen flowing from India into the US is unmatched, Gor added. "And for US companies, India is a big market."Also Read: India-US trade talks hit a plateau as FM flags tough road aheadTechnology was among the strongest pillars of the US-India relationship, he said, citing investments by major American companies in India’s data centre and semiconductor industries.“If you look at IT, it’s unmatched. Google, Microsoft Adobe, Micron, every one of them is opening data centres, chip manufacturing here,” Gor said.He described the relationship as mutually beneficial, with investment and manufacturing activity in India supporting economic opportunities in the US as well. “So when a job is great in India, a counter job is created in the US. And so, it’s an incredible win-win situation. There’s not a lot of countries in the world that have this kind of potential.”

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has flagged an “undesirable incident” involving the alleged use of AI-generated, non-existent judgments in a compilation of cases submitted on behalf of the appellants, expressing concern over the conduct of the lawyers involved in the matter.
A Bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih, while dismissing appeals filed by GSTAAD Hotels Pvt.
and Neo Capricorn Plaza Pvt.
against the initiation of insolvency proceedings against them, recorded that the respondents had immediately objected to the compilation, alleging that it contained judgments that did not exist.

“When queried by the Court, the Advocate-on-Record for the appellants sought to shift the entire blame on the appellants while at the same time feigning ignorance of what the compilation contained,” the Court observed.
The judgment further recorded that senior counsel appearing for the appellants subsequently took responsibility for the incident and sought forgiveness on behalf of the appellants.

The Court had initially considered imposing exemplary costs but, after being informed of the death of the first appellant, deleted the proposed costs and directed that there would be no order as to costs.

The Court made these observations while deciding appeals filed by the companies challenging the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal's decision upholding the admission of insolvency petitions under Section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC).

On the merits, the Supreme Court held that at the admission stage of an insolvency petition, a financial creditor is required to establish the occurrence of default through a summary assessment of documentary evidence and need not prove the exact outstanding liability after an exhaustive reconciliation of the corporate debtor's accounts.
“The trigger for initiation of the CIRP is the occurrence of a default, not the final adjudication of the creditor's entire claim,” the Court said.

The Bench clarified that disputes over the precise amount of outstanding debt, including the computation of interest, penal charges or other accounting entries, do not negate an established default or prevent admission of a Section 7 application, provided the statutory threshold under Section 4 of the IBC is satisfied.

“The standard applicable at the admission stage is one of preponderance of probabilities upon the documentary material placed on record,” the Court observed, adding that the threshold was deliberately modest and required a summary, prima facie finding of financial debt and default rather than a full trial into disputed facts.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has observed that it would be “highly unfair” to make investors bear the consequences of administrative lapses, after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) allegedly allowed YES Bank's Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio to fall to 0.6% despite earlier irregularities in the bank's functioning.
“The RBI was a mere bystander, allowing the CET1 ratio of YES BANK to drop to an astonishing low of 0.6% while the business of YES BANK was being carried out in a clandestine manner.
It cannot be denied that material irregularities in functioning of YES BANK were noticed much prior; criminal prosecution has also been initiated against the personnel of YES BANK.

However, to have the investors at the receiving end of the administrative lapses would be highly unfair.”, a bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih observed while setting aside the write-down of ₹8,415 crore worth of Additional Tier 1 (AT-1) bonds.
The Court upheld the Bombay High Court's decision, holding that YES Bank's Administrator lacked the authority to write down the bonds after the final reconstruction scheme came into force.
“…administrator appointed under the BR Act has to act squarely within the four corners of the powers conferred upon him under the statute.
He acts as a substitute for the Board of Directors, to run the company in an efficient manner.

Any act performed by the administrator beyond the powers clothed upon him would be wholly illegal and void.”, the Court said, emphasizing that an Administrator cannot be said to have exercised the power vested in the RBI.
The Court noted that material irregularities in YES Bank's functioning had been noticed much earlier and criminal prosecution had also been initiated against bank personnel.
However, it said investors could not be made to bear the consequences of administrative failures.
Although the draft reconstruction scheme expressly provided for a permanent write-down of AT-1 bonds, the clause was omitted from the final scheme notified on March 13, 2020.
The Administrator nevertheless wrote down the bonds the next day, extinguishing investors' claims.

stories.title: India’s merchandise exports climb 23% to $44.4 bn in September
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 15 : India's merchandise exports recorded a robust 23.04 per cent growth year-on-year to touch a four-month high of $44.4 billion in September this year, despite the uncertainties in global markets and the disruption in shipping due to the escalating Middle East conflict, official figures released on Thursday showed. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal said the growth trend in India's exports was continuing, indicating sustained momentum in outbound shipments. The growth in goods exports was driven by a broad-based increase in shipments across sectors, with particularly strong growth in petroleum products, meat, dairy and poultry products, handicrafts, and some cereals, he added. Imports rose 8 per cent to $74.61 billion during the month due to the increase in prices of crude oil in the global market. The surge in exports also led to a narrowing of the trade deficit to $30.21 billion during the month on a year-on-year basis from around $33 billion recorded in September 2025. However, on a sequential basis, the trade deficit was higher than the corresponding figure of $26.86 billion in the previous month of August. Cumulatively, goods exports stood at $259.89 billion during April-September, up nearly 19 per cent year-on-year. Imports rose 16 per cent year-on-year to $437.53 billion in the first six months of financial year 2026-27 (FY27). As a result, the merchandise trade deficit stood at $177.64 billion during the six-month period. Strong growth in merchandise exports has also increased their contribution to gross domestic product (GDP), after the share of exports recorded a consistent decline over the past three financial years. Exports accounted for 14 per cent of GDP in the first quarter of FY27, the latest figures show. Following a slowdown in global demand in FY24 and FY25, and the uncertainties triggered by the US tariff turmoil in FY26, the share of exports in GDP declined to 11.3 per cent in FY26 from 11.7 per cent in FY25. --IANS

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has held that a person having parted with his share in a property via a compromise deed cannot later execute a gift deed in relation to the same property.

The Court faulted the Telangana High Court's order for overlooking a compromise deed before upholding the execution of a gift deed by a man who had already relinquished his share via a compromise deed.

A bench of Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva heard a case in which a man, despite having relinquished his claim over properties allotted to his mother under a 1986 compromise in exchange for absolute rights over a house property, subsequently executed a gift deed in 2007 in respect of the same properties.

The core legal issue before the Court was whether a gift deed could be upheld without properly appreciating the effect of an earlier family settlement and a compromise decree that had recognised the parties' respective rights over the properties.
The dispute arose from a family settlement executed on April 19, 1959, dividing ancestral properties among family members.
Under the settlement, Madhusudhan Reddy received specific properties, while certain lands in Karkalpahad village were allotted to his mother, Manikyamma.
Subsequently, during the pendency of litigation concerning the family properties, Madhusudhan Reddy entered into a compromise with Anasuyamma and her adopted son, Venkatraji Reddy, in February 1986.
Under the settlement, he relinquished his claim over the properties allotted to his mother and secured absolute rights over the Himayatnagar house.
The compromise was recorded by the High Court, which allowed the appeal in terms of the settlement in September 1990.
However, in April 2007, Madhusudhan Reddy executed a registered gift deed in favour of Siddhartha Reddy, transferring several parcels of land in Karkalpahad village.

The appellants contended that the lands covered by the deed had not been allotted to Madhusudhan Reddy under the 1959 family settlement and were among the properties over which he had relinquished his claims under the 1986 compromise.

Anasuyamma, Venkatraji Reddy and another family member subsequently filed a suit seeking a declaration of title, a declaration that the gift deed was null and void, mutation of revenue records and a permanent injunction.

article_sentences: Amid deep factionalism in the Punjab Congress and ahead of the Assembly election, newly appointed Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) chief Pargat Singh on Saturday (October 3, 2026) drew on his experience as former captain of the Indian hockey team, and stressed the importance of team spirit and being a team player.
Replacing Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, who headed the party’s Punjab unit for more than four years, Mr. Singh repeatedly used the language of sport to underline his approach to the job.
“I have been a team player,” he told reporters here, adding that he had always played as a “full-back” — a position centred on supporting the team from behind.
“I feel there are very good players in our team.
We will take all decisions unanimously,” he said, in a clear attempt to reach out to the party’s competing factions and senior leaders.
He recast the gaze from internal differences to the larger political context in Punjab.
“The issue is Punjab and not differences amongst us,” he said, while describing Mr. Warring as a “player of our team”.
He also said that all the senior leaders would be ahead of him in the team.
“We are a team.
This is Rahul Gandhi’s team,” Mr. Singh said, adding that the Congress would pursue “constructive politics” and seek to “revive democracy”.

His emphasis on cohesion comes at a politically difficult moment for the Punjab Congress, which has been marked by factional differences as the party prepares for the Assembly election, due early next year.

Mr. Singh, who called on the All India Congress Committee general secretary in-charge of Punjab, Sachin Pilot, stressed on building a “very good team in Punjab” and gave a call to those who had left the Congress to return if they wanted to contribute to the State.

stories.headline: India Cements acquires 3.6% stake in Zenataris Renewable for captive power needs
stories.title: India Cements acquires 3.6% stake in Zenataris Renewable for captive power needs
stories.summary: The consideration involved is an equity investment of over Rs ₹20 crore and it will be closed within 120 days from the execution of the agreement
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India Cements on Thursday said that the company has entered into energy supply and share subscription agreement to acquire 3.62 per cent equity shares of Zenataris Renewable Energy Private Ltd, a company engaged in generation and transmission of renewable energy.

“The acquisition is for the purposes of meeting India Cements’ green energy needs, optimising energy cost and comply with regulatory requirements for captive power consumption under electricity laws,” the company said in a filing to the exchanges.
The consideration involved is an equity investment of over ₹20 crore and it will be closed within 120 days from the execution of the agreement.

Zenataris is based in Hyderabad, and is a special purpose vehicle (SPV) established for the development and operation of Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) hybrid renewable energy project located at Kudligi, Vijayanagara District, Karnataka.
The SPV shall supply 11 MW renewable energy to the cement plants of India Cements on a group captive basis, a statement filed by India Cements to the exchanges said.

stories.headline: Jio's Akash Ambani says services, not tariff hikes, to drive revenue as record IPO nears
stories.title: Jio's Akash Ambani says services, not tariff hikes, to drive revenue as record IPO nears
stories.summary: Ambani said Jio charges about Rs 4.9 per gigabyte against an industry average of Rs 7.5, with customers using 43.7 GB a month.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Ambani said Jio charges about Rs 4.9 per gigabyte against an industry average of Rs 7.5, with customers using 43.7 GB a month.

Jio Platforms plans to raise revenue per customer mainly by selling more services rather than lifting tariffs, though it keeps the option of higher prices, Managing Director Akash Ambani said on Thursday, days before the Reliance Industries unit opens what would be India's largest initial public offering.

"We always have the ability to take up prices," Ambani told a press conference in Mumbai, but the company would rather give customers more services and charge for them than rely on price per gigabyte as its main lever.
Asked whether a tariff increase was coming, he gave no timeline.
He said telecom spending per user as a share of India's per-capita income had roughly halved to about 1% since Jio's 2016 launch, which he called headroom.
Chief Executive Pankaj Pawar said tariffs were only one of several levers.

"We expect a USD 1.4-trillion digital economy by FY31; we will take a huge market share of this," Ambani said, naming mobile, home broadband and enterprise and international services as the growth engines.
He said Jio carries more than 60% of India's wireless data traffic.
New services outside Jio's licensed telecom business, such as a voice-AI feature announced at Reliance's annual meeting, could push its EBITDA margin above the current level.
The margin was 53.3 per cent in April-June, up from about 50% three years ago, he added.

On overseas expansion, Ambani said Jio would offer its in-house network technology to foreign operators as a managed-service partner, not by selling hardware or software licences, and without heavy capital spending.
He said the split between domestic and international revenue would become clear "as we sign on our first customers".
